chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Abu al-Jarrah Talhah ibn Zayd from al-Fadl ibn 'Uthman al-A'war from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who is killed and his head is found in a tribe, he said: 'His blood money is upon whoever is found in his tribe with his chest and hands, and the prayer is performed over him.'

key_terms.وَالصَّلَاةُ عَلَيْهِ: And the prayer is performed over him (funeral prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for performing funeral prayer and paying blood money when only the head and hands of a deceased man are found within a tribe?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the criteria for tribal liability in *diyah* (blood money) when a victim's identity is partially established by the presence of the chest and hands within a tribe's territory, even if the head is found there. It underscores the practical application of collective responsibility in early Islamic jurisprudence and links the financial compensation directly to the performance of the funeral prayer (*Salat al-Mayyit*), emphasizing the deceased's continued communal standing.
